content: While small-scale studies of dehumanization and media representation of marginalized communities provide valuable insights (e.g. BIBREF10), there exist no known large-scale analyses, likely due to difficulties in quantifying such a subjective and multidimensional psychological process. However, the ability to do large-scale analysis is crucial for understanding how dehumanizing attitudes have evolved over long periods of time. Furthermore, by being able to account for a greater amount of media discourse at once, large-scale techniques can provide a more complete view of the media environment to which the public is exposed.
